text: In Shannon's sense, how much information do you gain from learning the result of flipping a two-headed coin?
choices: None, because the outcome was already certain
One bit, because a coin flip is by definition one bit
Half a bit, because only one outcome is possible
One bit, because the coin has two faces
explanation: Shannon defines a bit as the information gained by resolving a question whose outcomes were equally likely. A two-headed coin has a certain outcome, so learning it resolves nothing. The tempting answers apply the everyday shorthand 'a coin flip is one bit' without checking the equally-likely condition the definition actually requires — a distinction that becomes the basis of compression in Unit VIII.
